title_en: The Stink That Built London's Sewers
english_paragraphs: In the fierce heat of summer 1858, the curtains of the new Houses of Parliament hung heavy with chloride of lime, a bleach to make the air tolerable. The Thames festered, and MPs contemplated moving out.

The river had become London's lavatory. Antiquated sewers and outlets discharged the untreated sewage of some three million city dwellers into its currents, where the excrement stewed and decayed. The vile fumes grew so overpowering that the episode earned a name, the Great Stink.

Disgust found a voice on 15 July, when the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Benjamin Disraeli, denounced the river as a hellish pool of unbearable horrors. A bill funding new sewers was fast-tracked into law in about 18 days.

The engineer Joseph Bazalgette masterminded the response. His 82 miles of stout intercepting sewers caught the flow short of the river and diverted it east, downstream of the city. With some 1,100 miles of street sewers as tributaries, the infrastructure took 318 million bricks. Having calculated an adequate calibre for each pipe, he doubled it. The backbone lies buried underneath the newly built Victoria, Albert, and Chelsea Embankments. Substantially complete by 1875, much of the network is in use today.

Yet that sanitation rested on a fallacy. The predominant belief, miasma, blamed disease on foul air and vapours, so the sewers were intended principally to suppress the smell. They worked for an unintended reason, guarding the purity of the water Londoners drank.
Cholera resurfaced in 1866 and killed about 5,600 people in the East End, the one locality not yet connected.
A remedy aimed at the nose protected the gut.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 在**酷热**(fierce heat)的1858年夏天，新落成的**议会大厦**(Houses of Parliament)里的窗帘垂挂着，沉甸甸地浸湿了氯化**石灰**(lime)，这是一种**漂白剂**(bleach)，用来让空气变得**可以忍受**(tolerable)。泰晤士河正在**溃烂发臭**(festered)，而议员们**考虑**(contemplated)过搬离这里。

这条河已经成了伦敦的**厕所**(lavatory)。**老旧的**(Antiquated)下水道和**排污口**(outlets)**排放**(discharged)**未经处理的**(untreated)**污水**(sewage)，它们来自约三百万城市**居民**(dwellers)，排入河的**水流**(currents)中，在那里，**粪便**(excrement)**处于炎热的空气中**(stewed)并**腐败**(decayed)。**令人恶心的**(vile)**刺鼻气体**(fumes)变得如此**极其强烈的/令人难以忍受**(overpowering)，以至于**这段时期**(episode)赢得了一个名字，大**恶臭**(Stink)。

这股**厌恶**(Disgust)找到了代言人，是在7月15日，当时**财政大臣**(Chancellor of the Exchequer)本杰明·迪斯雷利**公开抨击**(denounced as)这条河**是**(denounced as)一潭**地狱般的**(hellish)池水，满是**令人无法忍受的**(unbearable)恐怖。一项为新下水道拨款的**法案**(bill)**被快速推进/被加速审批**(fast-tracked)，成为法律，只用了约18天。

工程师约瑟夫·巴泽尔杰特**主持策划了**(masterminded)这次应对。他修建的82英里**坚固的**(stout)**截流下水道**(intercepting sewers)截住了污水，**在到达**(short of)河流**之前**(short of)，并把它**改道**(diverted)向东，送往城市**下游**(downstream)。有约1,100英里的街道下水道作为**支流**(tributaries)，整套**基础设施**(infrastructure)用了三亿一千八百万**砖块**(bricks)。先算出**足够的**(adequate)**内径/粗细**(calibre)，用于每条管道，他再把它**加倍**(doubled)。系统的**主干**(backbone)就**埋藏**(buried)在**新近**(newly)修成的维多利亚、阿尔伯特和切尔西河堤**之下**(underneath)。到1875年**基本上**(Substantially)已经完工，这套管网的大部分至今仍**在使用**(in use)。

然而，这套**卫生设施/下水道设施**(sanitation)**建立在**(rested on)一个**谬误**(fallacy)**之上**(rested on)。当时**占主导地位的**(predominant)**看法**(belief)是瘴气说，把疾病归咎于**污浊的空气**(foul air)和臭水的**蒸汽**(vapours)，所以下水道修建的目的**主要**(principally)是为了**压住**(suppress)臭味。它们奏效，却是出于一个**意料之外的**(unintended)原因，那就是守住了伦敦人饮用水的**洁净**(purity)。
霍乱**再次出现**(resurfaced)于1866年，夺去了约5,600人的生命，在伦敦东区，那是唯一尚未接入的**地区**(locality)。
一项**冲着**(aimed at)鼻子**去的**(aimed at)补救措施，护住的却是**肠胃**(gut)。

sentences.english: In the fierce heat of summer 1858, the curtains of the new Houses of Parliament hung heavy with chloride of lime, a bleach to make the air tolerable.
sentences.chinese_source: 在**酷热**(fierce heat)的1858年夏天，新落成的**议会大厦**(Houses of Parliament)里的窗帘垂挂着，沉甸甸地浸湿了氯化**石灰**(lime)，这是一种**漂白剂**(bleach)，用来让空气变得**可以忍受**(tolerable)。

sentences.english: The Thames festered, and MPs contemplated moving out.
sentences.chinese_source: 泰晤士河正在**溃烂发臭**(festered)，而议员们**考虑**(contemplated)过搬离这里。

sentences.english: The river had become London's lavatory.
sentences.chinese_source: 这条河已经成了伦敦的**厕所**(lavatory)。

sentences.english: Antiquated sewers and outlets discharged the untreated sewage of some three million city dwellers into its currents, where the excrement stewed and decayed.
sentences.chinese_source: **老旧的**(Antiquated)下水道和**排污口**(outlets)**排放**(discharged)**未经处理的**(untreated)**污水**(sewage)，它们来自约三百万城市**居民**(dwellers)，排入河的**水流**(currents)中，在那里，**粪便**(excrement)**处于炎热的空气中**(stewed)并**腐败**(decayed)。

sentences.english: The vile fumes grew so overpowering that the episode earned a name, the Great Stink.
sentences.chinese_source: **令人恶心的**(vile)**刺鼻气体**(fumes)变得如此**极其强烈的/令人难以忍受**(overpowering)，以至于**这段时期**(episode)赢得了一个名字，大**恶臭**(Stink)。

sentences.english: Disgust found a voice on 15 July, when the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Benjamin Disraeli, denounced the river as a hellish pool of unbearable horrors.
sentences.chinese_source: 这股**厌恶**(Disgust)找到了代言人，是在7月15日，当时**财政大臣**(Chancellor of the Exchequer)本杰明·迪斯雷利**公开抨击**(denounced as)这条河**是**(denounced as)一潭**地狱般的**(hellish)池水，满是**令人无法忍受的**(unbearable)恐怖。

sentences.english: A bill funding new sewers was fast-tracked into law in about 18 days.
sentences.chinese_source: 一项为新下水道拨款的**法案**(bill)**被快速推进/被加速审批**(fast-tracked)，成为法律，只用了约18天。

sentences.english: The engineer Joseph Bazalgette masterminded the response.
sentences.chinese_source: 工程师约瑟夫·巴泽尔杰特**主持策划了**(masterminded)这次应对。

sentences.english: His 82 miles of stout intercepting sewers caught the flow short of the river and diverted it east, downstream of the city.
sentences.chinese_source: 他修建的82英里**坚固的**(stout)**截流下水道**(intercepting sewers)截住了污水，**在到达**(short of)河流**之前**(short of)，并把它**改道**(diverted)向东，送往城市**下游**(downstream)。

sentences.english: With some 1,100 miles of street sewers as tributaries, the infrastructure took 318 million bricks.
sentences.chinese_source: 有约1,100英里的街道下水道作为**支流**(tributaries)，整套**基础设施**(infrastructure)用了三亿一千八百万**砖块**(bricks)。

sentences.english: Having calculated an adequate calibre for each pipe, he doubled it.
sentences.chinese_source: 先算出**足够的**(adequate)**内径/粗细**(calibre)，用于每条管道，他再把它**加倍**(doubled)。

sentences.english: The backbone lies buried underneath the newly built Victoria, Albert, and Chelsea Embankments.
sentences.chinese_source: 系统的**主干**(backbone)就**埋藏**(buried)在**新近**(newly)修成的维多利亚、阿尔伯特和切尔西河堤**之下**(underneath)。

sentences.english: Substantially complete by 1875, much of the network is in use today.
sentences.chinese_source: 到1875年**基本上**(Substantially)已经完工，这套管网的大部分至今仍**在使用**(in use)。

sentences.english: Yet that sanitation rested on a fallacy.
sentences.chinese_source: 然而，这套**卫生设施/下水道设施**(sanitation)**建立在**(rested on)一个**谬误**(fallacy)**之上**(rested on)。

sentences.english: The predominant belief, miasma, blamed disease on foul air and vapours, so the sewers were intended principally to suppress the smell.
sentences.chinese_source: 当时**占主导地位的**(predominant)**看法**(belief)是瘴气说，把疾病归咎于**污浊的空气**(foul air)和臭水的**蒸汽**(vapours)，所以下水道修建的目的**主要**(principally)是为了**压住**(suppress)臭味。

sentences.english: They worked for an unintended reason, guarding the purity of the water Londoners drank.
sentences.chinese_source: 它们奏效，却是出于一个**意料之外的**(unintended)原因，那就是守住了伦敦人饮用水的**洁净**(purity)。

sentences.english: Cholera resurfaced in 1866 and killed about 5,600 people in the East End, the one locality not yet connected.
sentences.chinese_source: 霍乱**再次出现**(resurfaced)于1866年，夺去了约5,600人的生命，在伦敦东区，那是唯一尚未接入的**地区**(locality)。

approved_summary: 1858年酷暑，伦敦未经处理的污水在泰晤士河发臭，恶臭逼得议员考虑搬离议会。
财政大臣公开抨击后，为新下水道拨款的法案约18天获通过，工程师巴泽尔杰特主持建设。
82英里截流管拦下原本入河的污水，改送城市下游；按需要算出的管径再加倍。
修下水道本为消除人们误认为会致病的臭气；实际作用是减少饮用水遭污水污染。
1866年，唯一尚未接网的东区有约5600人死于霍乱；管网1875年基本完工，多数设施至今仍用。
